h1: InterContinental Hua Hin Resort — beachfront in town, with the beach and the mall on your doorstep
intro: If you want a genuine luxury beachfront resort in Hua Hin but don't want to leave the convenience of town behind — InterContinental Hua Hin Resort nails it, sitting right on Hua Hin Beach in the centre of town on Petchkasem Road, directly opposite the BluPort shopping mall. It's a 5-star IHG resort with 159 rooms and suites split between a seafront Beach Wing and a wing by the mall. What guests mention most is the beachfront pool, the breakfast and the staff service. From approx. THB 5,500/night. Scored 9.2 from 176 reviews.

body.html: InterContinental Hua Hin Resort sits directly on Hua Hin Beach in the centre of town on Petchkasem Road, right opposite the BluPort shopping mall. That's what sets it apart from luxury resorts you have to drive out of town to reach — step out the back and you're on the beach; cross the road and you're at a mall with restaurants, a supermarket and a cinema. It suits travellers who want both seaside luxury and the convenience of walking out to eat, shop and explore without relying on a car all the time.

The 159 rooms are split across two main zones. The Beach Wing is the seafront side, with around 119 rooms and suites, many with garden or sea views, while the wing by the mall (BluPort/Garden Wing) has around 40 modern rooms and its own pool. The rooms lean warm and contemporary, with beds guests often praise as comfortable. Worth knowing: some rooms feel a little dated for the price point, so ask for a renovated room if newness matters to you.

"Swim in the beachfront pool in the morning looking out over the long sweep of Hua Hin Beach, walk over for breakfast by the sea — then cross the road to the mall to escape the afternoon heat. It really is all in one place."

The heart of it is the wide, sea-view beachfront pool, with sun loungers lining the sand and a pool bar. Many guests say the pool-and-beach zone is somewhere you can spend the whole day. The stretch of Hua Hin Beach in front of the resort is fine sand you can stroll for a long way, and you'll still see the classic Hua Hin horseback rides along the shore. There's also the SPA InterContinental with warm hardwood accents, a 24-hour fitness centre, and the Planet Trekkers kids' club for families.

Dining spans four restaurants and two bars. The breakfast buffet is the most-talked-about thing in reviews — varied, fresh, and well looked after by the team. The seaside restaurant serves seafood and international dishes in a breezy setting to the sound of the waves. One note from some reviews: the menu leans heavily on seafood, which can limit variety on a longer stay, and on weekends breakfast gets busy enough that seating fills up.

The location is a clear strength. It's in central Hua Hin within reach of the night market and walking street, close to Hua Hin railway station and Chatchai Market. Hua Hin Airport is about 10–15 minutes by car, and Bangkok is around a 3-hour drive. It scores 9.2 from 176 Trip.com reviews, with an especially high location score — reflecting how much guests value having both the beach and the convenience of town in one spot.

Honestly, the thing to accept is that being in the centre of town beside a main road and a mall means it isn't as quiet and private as an out-of-town resort. Some reviews note that parking is limited, the pool-bar service can be slow at times, and a few rooms are far from the lobby or have dim walkway lighting at night. But if what you want is a luxury beachfront resort that's easy to walk anywhere from, is pet-friendly in some wings, and delivers IHG-level service — this place does it in a way that's hard to match in central Hua Hin.

A tip from following the reviews here for a while: for the full seaside feel, ask for a Beach Wing room near the pool and beach; if you're after the convenience of walking to the mall or bringing a pet, the BluPort wing suits better. In high season and over long weekends (December–February and public holidays) rates climb noticeably and the best-view rooms sell out fast, so book ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate first, then compare prices across platforms.

honestSummary: InterContinental Hua Hin Resort is best for travellers chasing a luxury beachfront resort you can still walk into town from to eat and shop — beachfront in central Hua Hin opposite the BluPort mall, with a fine sea-view pool, well-rated breakfast, and pet-friendly rooms in some wings. But accept that the in-town location means it isn't as quiet and private, and some rooms feel dated.
honestChecks: If you're after a quiet, private hide-from-the-world resort — this is in the centre of town beside a main road and mall, livelier than an out-of-town resort → if calm is the point, consider a resort around Khao Takiab or Pranburi instead.
If you're particular about brand-new rooms — some rooms feel a little dated for the price → ask for a renovated room or a higher-tier suite when booking, and check real room photos before confirming.

If it's high season or a long weekend (Dec–Feb) and you haven't booked — rates rise fast and the best-view rooms go early → book ahead with a free-cancellation rate, then compare prices across platforms.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — InterContinental Hua Hin Resort

faq.q: Where is InterContinental Hua Hin Resort and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 33/33 Petchkasem Road, directly on Hua Hin Beach in the centre of town, right opposite the BluPort shopping mall. You can walk straight to the beach and cross to the mall in 2 minutes. The night market, Hua Hin railway station and Chatchai Market are about 6–7 minutes by car, Hua Hin Airport about 12 minutes, and Bangkok roughly a 3-hour drive.

faq.q: How much does InterContinental Hua Hin Resort cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 5,500/night for a Cosy Room in the BluPort wing. From there you can step up to a Premium Ocean View, a King Premium Pool View (54 sqm), and a Single Private Pool Suite (63 sqm with a private plunge pool) at around THB 15,000. High-season and long-weekend rates rise noticeably — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is InterContinental Hua Hin Resort best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for travellers who want a luxury beachfront resort while still being able to walk into town to eat and shop. It suits couples, families (there's a kids' club), and pet owners (pet-friendly in some wings). If a quiet, private hide-from-the-world feel is what you want, an out-of-town resort may suit you better.

faq.q: Is InterContinental Hua Hin Resort pet-friendly?
faq.a: Yes, in some wings (the BluPort Wing and villas), with conditions on weight, number and length of stay — generally up to 2 pets per booking and under around 20 kg, with dedicated pet facilities. Always notify the hotel and check the latest conditions before booking.

faq.q: What are the beach and pool like at InterContinental Hua Hin Resort?
faq.a: It's a true beachfront resort right on Hua Hin Beach; the sand in front is fine and good for long strolls, and you'll still see the classic Hua Hin horseback rides along the shore. The beachfront pool is wide with good views, loungers and a pool bar, and each wing has its own pool. Many guests say it's somewhere you can happily spend the whole day.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book, and is cancellation flexible?
faq.a: In high season (December–February) and over long weekends, book 1–2 months ahead, as rates climb and the best-view rooms sell out fast. Other times, 2–3 weeks is usually fine. Every platform offers a Free Cancellation option — choose that first if your plans aren't firm, then compare prices across a few sites.
